body.statement: The legal observed-law image \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is compact and semialgebraic. For each \(n\), the graph over \(\widehat p\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) of \(\widehat p\mapsto\{b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\|b-\widehat p\|_\infty\le a_n\}\) is compact and semialgebraic; for each fixed \(r>0\), the graph of \(p\mapsto\mathcal B(p,r)\) is compact and semialgebraic. Consequently definable optimization makes \(T_n(g)\) and \(E_{p,r}(g)\) finite Borel value functions of all displayed arguments. With \(G^*=\Sigma(\widehat p_n)^{1/2}W^*\) and the lower-quantile convention, \(c_n\) and the total rectangle \(C_n\) are measurable.
body.justification: The confidence procedure requires finite optimizers and a measurable conditional critical value on every empirical law.
body.gap: Directional-bootstrap papers typically impose measurability of the derivative process rather than deriving it from this finite legal semialgebraic image.
body.consumer: The theorem-level rectangle becomes a genuine statistic suitable for simulation and coverage analysis.
